history.dynasty: None (sub-shrine within the Yadadri temple complex; no independent founding is documented)
history.period: Hill temple with Tretayuga legendary associations; complex rebuilt 2016-2022
history.summary: IDENTITY FLAG: no standalone, independently documented 'Hanuman Temple' at Yadagirigutta was found. The best-supported referent is the Anjaneya/Hanuman shrine at the entrance of the Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy temple on Yadadri hill - 'to the right of the temple main door is a Hanuman temple' (Wikipedia), and Hanuman is venerated as the kshetra palaka (guardian/ruler) of the hill (orientalzenz). Temple legend says sage Yadarishi performed penance on this hill with the blessings of Anjaneya (Hanuman) before Lord Narasimha appeared before him in five forms; a rock carving of Hanuman also stands on the old hill. The 2016-2022 reconstruction (inaugurated 28 March 2022) deliberately left the Anjaneya Swamy statue near the entrance undisturbed (Atlantis Press engineering paper). Smaller shrines to Hanuman are also listed among the sub-shrines of the renovated complex. Coordinates below are those of the main temple complex, provisional for the shrine itself.

name: Hanuman Temple, Yadagirigutta
town_description: Yadagirigutta (now often called Yadadri) is a temple town in Yadadri Bhuvanagiri district, Telangana, about 60 km from Hyderabad, famous for the hilltop Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy temple (Pancha Narasimha Kshetra, one of two Nava Narasimha Kshetras in Telangana). The renovated complex (inaugurated 2022) sprawls over several acres on the hillock and is a major pilgrimage destination.

travel.airport: Rajiv Gandhi International Airport, Hyderabad - about 90-100 km (verify).
travel.railway: Nearest stations are on the Secunderabad-Kazipet line (Raigir/Bhongir side) - about 10-15 km (verify).
travel.road: About 60 km from Hyderabad on NH-163; state buses run to the hilltop free of charge (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Brahmotsavam (Feb-Mar) is the major festival period.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Main temple listed as 4:00 AM - 3:00 PM and 4:00 PM - 9:45 PM (verify - applies to the host complex, not the Hanuman shrine specifically).
